title: Recursion
misconceptions: Recursive calls share the exact same stack frame, parameters, and local variables.
A recursive function without a base case will run forever without crashing.
Reaching the base case instantly returns the final answer to the original caller without unwinding previous recursive calls.
Recursive calls solve larger or equal-sized instances of the original problem.

rubric.text: Defines recursion as a function calling itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem.
Explains that a base case is the condition where the function stops calling itself and returns a value directly.
States that omitting a base case causes the function to never stop calling itself.
Explains that each recursive call adds a new stack frame to the call stack containing its own parameters and local variables.
Describes stack unwinding as the step-by-step process where recursive calls return one by one after reaching the base case.
Explains that excessively deep recursion exhausts available call stack space and causes a stack overflow crash.
Uses the factorial function where factorial(n) = n * factorial(n - 1) with base case factorial(0) = 1 to demonstrate recursion.
